title: Product PRD: Unified Inference - Pricing & Packaging
author: Marina Lopez
abstract: This PRD defines pricing and packaging options for Redwood's Unified Inference product line (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to provide clear, predictable economics for customers while retaining levers for enterprise contracts and reserved capacity. This doc covers target segments, proposed SKUs, unit economics, migration incentives, and rollout plan.
background: Redwood's Unified Inference unifies hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes under a consistent API and operational model. Customers have requested simpler packaging for mixed workloads (bursty public endpoints + steady reserved capacity) and clearer guidance on when to use Dedicated vs Hosted. The company also needs pricing that supports PLG motion while enabling sales to negotiate enterprise commitments.
goals: Provide simple, tiered hosted SKUs that scale from developer to production teams
Define Reserved Capacity bundles and overage rules for Dedicated
Offer a clear private deployment license and support tiers for regulated customers
Align pricing with cost drivers: GPU-hours, memory footprint, quantization/efficiency profiles, and request concurrency
Preserve unit economics and win rate targets: gross margin >= 65% for hosted, predictable ARR for Dedicated
non_goals: This doc does not specify exact per-token micropricing for every model variant (that will be managed in the rate-card backend)
It does not prescribe hardware-specific discounts (cloud provider/partner deals handled separately)
It does not finalize enterprise legal terms or SLAs; those remain in the contracts playbook
target_segments: Developer-first startups (low-to-moderate sustained usage; prefer hosted, self-serve)
Mid-market product teams (mix of hosted + reserved bursts; require quotas and team controls)
Enterprises & regulated customers (Dedicated or Private; require contractual SLAs, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integration)
proposed_hosted_skus: Starter (free tier + credits): up to 1M tokens/month, basic console, community support
Growth: pay-as-you-go pricing with volume discounts at 5B and 20B token thresholds; access to model catalog and batching recommendations
Business: committed spend discount, multi-seat console, longer logs retention, priority support
Enterprise: negotiated rates, custom quotas, audit retention, SOC2 & compliance add-ons
dedicated_pricing_model: Reserved capacity priced as a monthly GPU pool subscription with 3 term options (monthly, 12-month, 36-month). Pricing tiers map to GPU class (A100/H100-equivalent), pool size, and burstable capacity. Overage is charged at a reduced per-GPU-hour rate and can be throttled based on policy. Committed Annual Revenue (CAR) discounts apply for 12/36 month contracts.
private_deployment_pricing: Private deployments are licensed as a platform fee + annual support subscription. Platform fee tiers: Basic (single-region), Standard (multi-region), Enterprise (air-gapped option + compliance package). Support tiers: Bronze, Silver, Gold with 24/7 response and SLA options available in Gold.
unit_economics_and_assumptions: Key assumptions: average sequence length 64 tokens, model mix: 60% medium LLM (7B/13B), 30% large LLM (70B), 10% embeddings. GPU utilization targets: hosted 60% average, dedicated 85% average. Cost inputs include GPU amortization, power, instance infra, storage, and SRE/ops overhead. Target gross margins: hosted >= 65%, dedicated >= 55% on committed contracts.
requirements: Billing system integration to express both per-token usage and GPU-hour reserved lines on a single invoice
Console pricing page that displays estimated monthly cost for a given traffic profile
Rate-card API to return model-specific per-token and per-embedding prices depending on customer tier
Support for reserved capacity contracts and automatic discount application at commitment thresholds
Ability to configure burst capacity and define overage throttling policies per-customer
design_and_implementation_notes: Design must decouple pricing metadata from runtime routing so that customers can switch model variants without changing SKU. Implement a pricing-metadata service with immutable rate-card versions and a Price Simulator in Console that uses historical usage to estimate monthly spend. Analytics pipeline should emit token counts by model+route to feed the billing system. Ensure feature flags for staged rollout of new SKUs.
rollout_plan_and_timeline: Phase 1 (Q1 2026): Backend billing + rate-card API, Console price estimator, test with beta customers. Phase 2 (Q2 2026): Public launch of hosted tiers + reserved capacity purchase flow. Phase 3 (Q3 2026): Dedicated contract tooling, enterprise negotiation playbook, private deployment license packaging. Phase 4 (Q4 2026): Optimization passes on discounts, add-ons (longer retention, compliance packages) and partner marketplace listings.
roadmap_milestones: 2026-01: Complete rate-card API v1 and backfill historical usage
2026-03: Beta for Growth & Business hosted tiers with 10 pilot customers
2026-06: GA hosted SKUs and reserved capacity self-serve purchase
2026-09: Dedicated contract templates and partner marketplace listing
2026-11: Private deployment license packaging and compliance add-on GA
pricing_examples_and_calculator_notes: Example: A startup on Growth with 50M tokens/month (mixed models) is estimated at $X/month using the price estimator (showing per-token, per-embedding, and potential savings from batching). The Console price estimator supports 'traffic profile' presets (chat app, embedding pipeline, reranker) and returns a breakdown by model family, predicted GPU-hours, and suggested Reserved Capacity option.
migration_and_incentives: 6-month migration credits for Dedicated customers who sign a 12-month commit (credit applied over first 3 invoices)
Free data egress for first 90 days for Private deployments during onboarding
Model quantization advisory and optimization sessions for customers above $50k ARR
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Price complexity causes conversion friction. Mitigation: Clear UI, presets, and Sales calculator templates.
Risk: Underpriced reserved capacity hurts margins. Mitigation: conservative utilization assumptions and contractual minimums.
Risk: Billing discrepancies during rollout. Mitigation: dual-run mode and audit logs prior to deprecating legacy billing paths.
release_notes_summary: Initial public release of Unified Inference pricing and packaging. Highlights: new hosted SKUs (Starter, Growth, Business), Reserved Capacity self-serve buy flow, rate-card API v1, Console Price Estimator, and private deployment license tiers. Beta customers will be onboarded in March 2026 for feedback.
